newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine grain output to be record 52 mln T-gov't.
newsitem.headline: Argentine grain output to be record 52 mln T-gov't.

text.p: Argentine farmers are set to harvest a record 52 million tonnes of grains and oilseeds in 1996/97, seven million tonnes more than in 1995/96, Agriculture Secretariat Felipe Sola said Monday.

"We are heading for an absolute and historic record of more than 50 million tonnes, although this could depend a bit on the way the weather behaves," Sola said, quoted by the state-run Telam news agency.
Sola added that output should be seven million tonnes more than last season's 45 million tonnes, Telam reported.
He said that the increase in output was more due to human effort and spending than climatic luck.
"This is the product of a massive application of technology, despite the fact that the rains haven't accompanied us as much as we should have wished over the past few years," he said.
The trend to greater production has still to reach a plateau, according to Sola.
"We think that output will be 60 million tonnes by the year 2000," he said, adding that Argentine farming is becoming "more dynamic, with more investment, and more intensive."
